text.tspan: Everyday English - B2 - 2026/04/13 - Essay - 01
Furniture, light and space shape an everyday room.
Pexels · 13977663
Making a room your own
A good way to arrange a room combines practical structure with an awareness of other people. Neither a rigid plan nor
complete improvisation is sufficient on its own; both need to be judged in context.
The practical case is straightforward: giving everyday objects a clear place makes the room easier to use. Consider how we
keep keys in a bowl beside the door. The benefit is not merely efficiency. A modest arrangement prevents avoidable
confusion, leaving attention available for the activity itself rather than for problems that could have been anticipated.
Consideration adds a second, equally important dimension: small personal choices make a space feel familiar. In this
situation, we place a favourite photograph where we can see it from our chair. A decision can be convenient for one person
while creating difficulty for another, so its value depends partly on whose needs it recognises.
The most useful approach therefore brings structure and consideration together. Preparation establishes a workable starting
point; attention to other people keeps it responsive. Success should be assessed by how well the arrangement serves the
experience, rather than by how closely events follow the original plan.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a clear main idea; develop two different points with examples; bring them together in the
conclusion. Each body paragraph needs a distinct point and a concrete example. The conclusion should connect the
argument rather than introduce a new proposal.
Identify two obstacles that could arise when people arrange a room. Explain a workable response to each, rather than merely
listing the problems. Use four short paragraphs: introduction, two developed points, and conclusion.
